key_insight: Scale-aware composite forcing targets intermediate-scale motion and strengthens forward nonlinear energy transfer in lattice Boltzmann turbulence simulations.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers finer control of turbulent energy distribution than large-scale forcing alone, provided small-scale resolution remains adequate.
method: Combine large-scale random forcing with intermediate-scale velocity-aligned feedback.
Extract the target velocity field using composite filtering.
Compare feedback strengths of 1%–7% against baseline and enhanced large-scale forcing.
evidence_signal: At approximately matched dissipation rates, 5% feedback yields a 32.36% target-band energy fraction versus 27.55% for enhanced large-scale forcing, with 2.17–2.39 times greater post-transient forward flux across K = 12.
watch_item: Mean k_maxη falls to 1.01 at 5% feedback and 0.90 at 7%, indicating an approaching resolution limit and under-resolution risk, respectively.
paper_title: Scale-aware composite forcing enhances forward energy transfer in lattice Boltzmann simulations of forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence
